title: Shikumi benchmark record
description:
one measured build whose buckets, outcome and fixture agree with each other. it holds the
record as written, checked, so writing it out never regenerates or re-checks anything.

buckets.description:
where the wall time went, one bucket per kind of step, in step order. every step the
candidate's mechanism pays in the scenario has a bucket.

covered_ns.description:
the wall time at least one bucket's run covered, in nanoseconds; the rest went to work no
bucket names, such as scheduling and waiting.

graph_depth.description: the fixture's longest dependency chain, in edges. it must match the fixture.

incremental.description: whether rustc's incremental compilation was on; null for fixtures that run no compiler.

iteration.description: which repetition of the scenario this is, from 0.

nix.description:
the Nix implementation the candidate ran against; null when no Nix is in play, as for the
Cargo baseline.

started_at_unix_ms.description: when the measured build started, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

store_valid_paths.description: how many valid paths the store held when the build started; null when it wasn't read.

transport.description:
how work and outputs move between the candidate and the store; null when the candidate
has no store transport.

unit_count.description:
the units the fixture holds: crates for a Rust workspace, units for an overhead graph. it
must match the fixture.

wall_time_ns.description: elapsed wall-clock time of the measured build, in nanoseconds.

Bucket.description:
the time one kind of step took inside a measured build. offsets are from the instant the
build's timer started; when steps ran concurrently, `total_ns` sums them and can exceed the
span they cover.

count.description: how many times the step ran.

first_start_ns.description: when the first run of the step started, in nanoseconds after the timer started.

last_end_ns.description: when the last run of the step ended, in nanoseconds after the timer started.

total_ns.description: the summed duration of every run of the step, in nanoseconds.

version.description: the version line the candidate's tool reports.

ClientTrust.description:
what the daemon said about the client. a trusted client may override settings per connection,
so the record says which kind it was.

oneOf.description: the daemon didn't say, which older protocol versions and the CLI don't.

system_ns.description: system CPU time over the build, in nanoseconds.

user_ns.description: user CPU time over the build, in nanoseconds.

CpuScope.description: whose CPU time a record counts.

oneOf.description: the measured process and every child it waited for.

every CPU of the machine, which is the only scope that sees a daemon's work; it includes
whatever else ran meanwhile.

Fixture.description: what was built, with enough to regenerate it and a digest to prove the regeneration matches.

digest.description: the digest of the generated tree before any scenario edit.
the digest of the unit graph's canonical JSON.

Identifier.description: a lowercase name: a letter, then letters, digits and hyphens.

Identity.description:
a digest over each unit's name and output NAR hash, in unit order, beside the digest a
reference build of the same fixture state gave.

dependencies.description: how many of the other crates it depends on directly; at most `crates`.

arch.description: Rust's name for the CPU architecture, such as `x86_64` or `aarch64`.

cpu_model.description: the CPU model string; null where the platform doesn't report one.

name.description: the host's name, or the name given on the command line.

os.description: Rust's name for the operating system, such as `linux` or `macos`.

Mechanism.description: how a candidate runs a unit, which decides the steps it pays for.

oneOf.description: plain Cargo, in place, with its own target directory.
one derivation per unit, built by the daemon in its sandbox.
one derivation per batch of ready units, with one output per unit.
the executor runs the compiler in a sandbox it owns and adds outputs by content.
the store's own operations, which no executor changes: collection and registration.

NixEnvironment.description: where the Nix implementation ran, relative to the machine the record names.

oneOf.description: directly on the machine's own operating system.
inside a virtual machine on that machine.
inside a container on that machine.

NixImplementation.description:
the Nix a candidate ran against, with what distinguishes two runs of the same version: where it
ran, the settings that change what a build costs, and whether the daemon trusted the client.

version.description: the version the implementation reports, such as `2.95.4`.

NixSettings.description:
the settings that change what a build costs, as the implementation reported them for the run.
each is read rather than assumed: a run whose settings weren't read can't be told apart from
another, so the contract has no "unknown" value.

cores.description: cores offered to each build; 0 is Nix's own value for all of them.

use_cgroups.description: whether builds run in their own cgroups.

Outcome.description: the check a timed build has to pass: it did the work its row claims, and no more or less.

built.description: units whose compiler or builder ran.

expected_built.description: units the fixture's model says the scenario has to build.

identity.description:
the identity of every unit's output after the build, against a reference; null where
no reference exists, as for Cargo, whose outputs no other candidate produces.

output_bytes_sent.description: NAR bytes of unit outputs sent to the store, by re-addressing or adding them.

skipped.description: units found up to date without running anything.

source_bytes_sent.description: NAR bytes of unit sources sent to the store.

warm.description:
what an executor's incremental units started from; null when its units compile
without incremental state, and for Cargo, whose session is its own target directory.

bytes_received.description: NAR bytes received from the cache.

substituted.description: paths the store held after the substitution, out of those it was asked for.

deleted.description: unrooted unit paths no longer valid after the collection.

kept.description: rooted paths still valid after the collection.

registered.description: paths valid after the add, out of those sent.

RustWorkspaceParams.description:
the shape of a generated workspace. the types hold each count above zero; [`Self::validate`]
holds the rules between counts, and a record checks them when it's read.

crates.description: crates besides the large one, the hub included. must exceed `depth`.

dependencies_per_crate.description:
the most direct dependencies a crate takes: one from the layer below, the rest from any
lower layer.

depth.description: the longest dependency chain, in edges from a top-layer crate down to the hub.

generic_percent.description: the share of functions that are generic, so their code is generated in the calling crate.

large_crate.description: one crate much larger than the rest, for work below the crate; null for none.

oneOf.description: a build from an empty target directory, or of units none of which are in the store.
a build straight after a successful one, with nothing changed.
a build after one private function's body changed.
a build after a public signature changed in a crate many others depend on.

a build after an edit to the hub's crate directory that rustc never reads, so the rebuilt
unit's output is byte-identical and everything downstream has to be skipped.
a wide graph of do-nothing units, every one built: the fixed cost an executor adds per unit.

a chain of do-nothing units, every one built in turn: the latency an executor adds per
level of depth.

fetching every unit's sources and outputs, through their root manifest, from a local
binary cache into a store that has none of them.

collecting garbage in a store where rooted manifests keep some unit paths and the rest
are unrooted.
adding a batch of new content-addressed paths to the store.

Setting_SandboxMode.description: a setting's value for a run, or the fact that the implementation has no such setting.

Setting_boolean.description: a setting's value for a run, or the fact that the implementation has no such setting.

Setting_uint32.description: a setting's value for a run, or the fact that the implementation has no such setting.

Sha256.description: a SHA-256 digest in lowercase hex.

oneOf.description: independent units with no inputs, for throughput.
each unit takes the one before it as its only input, for latency.

Step.description:
a kind of step an executor pays for in a build. each is its own bucket, so a cost the product
would pay can't hide inside another step or outside the timer.

oneOf.description:
reading and writing the executor's own record of each unit's source and output, which a
no-op and an edit start from.
opening the executor's connections to the store, which every command pays again.
finding which unit sources changed: stats, reads and NAR hashing of the working tree.
adding changed unit sources to the store as content-addressed paths.
asking the store which paths are already valid.
computing `.drv` contents and paths in memory.
sending `.drv` files to the store.

a build request to the daemon, from send to reply: its sandbox setup and the builder
itself are inside, because the daemon reports neither apart.
re-adding built outputs at the content-addressed path their bytes give.
adding outputs an executor produced itself to the store by content.
writing the root manifest and registering its root.
setting up a sandbox the executor owns: namespaces, mounts and identity maps.
creating the process a unit runs in, up to the point its sandbox setup starts.
running the compiler or builder itself, from exec to exit.

a unit's warm incremental state outside the compile: recording the session it starts
from, counting what rustc reused, and canonicalizing the rlib an incremental build writes.
fetching paths from a binary cache into the store.
the daemon's garbage collection.
the worker protocol over the local daemon's unix socket.
the Nix command-line tools.
the worker protocol to `nix-daemon --stdio` over ssh.

Warm.description: the warm state an incremental build's units carried in.

reused.description: how many of those rustc took from the seeded session instead of rebuilding.

seeded.description: built units that started from a session of an earlier build.

work_products.description: object work products in the sessions the built units finalized.
